steps.name: Interaction DESeq2-equivalent model (PyDESeq2): interaction term and both simple effects
caveats: The interaction coefficient is a difference-of-differences with a larger standard error than either simple effect; at 4 replicates per cell, statistical power to detect the interaction is markedly lower than for either simple effect alone — state this directly wherever the interaction result is discussed, and do not equate a non-significant interaction with 'the drug acts the same in both genotypes'.

A gene significant in one simple-effect contrast but not flagged by the interaction test may still show a materially different effect size between genotypes that this design lacks power to formally call significant — report effect-size comparisons qualitatively alongside the formal interaction test.
steps.question: Within heart tissue, does the drug-vs-vehicle effect differ between WT and KO genotypes (interaction term), and what is the drug-vs-vehicle effect separately within WT and within KO?

grounding.reason: Interaction question with a 2x2 factorial design (R-0013) fit as DESeq2-equivalent Wald test with shrinkage (R-0001/R-0009); ashr side of the shrinkage dispute (R-0040/R-0009) is not available in Python, so the plan uses the relevel-to-single-coefficient approach so PyDESeq2's native apeglm-style shrinkage applies to all three quantities, and this substitution is stated as a flagged deviation from the sourced ashr recommendation.

constraints: Do not normalize or scale counts before fitting PyDESeq2 — normalization (median-of-ratios) is internal to the model.
Use only Python (PyDESeq2), not R/DESeq2/ashr/edgeR, for every script in this step, per user constraint.
Set genotype and treatment reference levels explicitly (WT, vehicle) rather than relying on alphabetical default level ordering; state the chosen references in every output table.
steps.description: Using the counts and metadata validated in T1S1, pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 raw counts in at least 4 samples (the smallest genotype x treatment cell size) — a minimal filter that does not replace PyDESeq2's independent filtering at the results step. Set genotype reference level explicitly to WT and treatment reference level explicitly to vehicle. Fit PyDESeq2 (median-of-ratios size factors estimated internally, no pre-normalization of counts) with design formula genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment (Model A, WT as genotype reference). Run a Wald test to extract two coefficients from Model A: the treatment (drug vs vehicle) effect within WT (the simple effect at the reference genotype level), and the genotype:treatment interaction coefficient (the difference-of-differences: how much more or less the drug effect is in KO relative to WT). Refit the identical design formula with genotype releveled so KO is the reference (Model B); from Model B, extract the treatment (drug vs vehicle) coefficient, which is the simple effect within KO. This two-model relevel approach yields all three quantities of interest as single fitted Wald coefficients, which lets PyDESeq2's native (Python, non-ashr) apeglm-style shrinkage apply uniformly. Apply lfc_shrink to each of the three coefficients (interaction, simple effect in WT, simple effect in KO) and report both the unshrunken log2FoldChange with its standard error and the shrunken log2FoldChange for every gene in every one of the three result tables; rank and plot on the shrunken value only. With 4 replicates per cell (below PyDESeq2's 7-replicate threshold for outlier replacement), Cook's-distance count outliers are flagged and their p-values set to NA rather than replaced — report the count of NA genes attributable to this flag separately from the count removed by independent filtering. Before trusting the adjusted p-values, plot and inspect the unadjusted p-value histogram for each of the three contrasts and report its shape. Produce MA plots (log2FoldChange vs mean normalized count, shrunken values, significant genes marked) and dispersion plots (per-gene, fitted trend, shrunken) as the two fit diagnostics for each of the two models. State explicitly that no second, independent DE method (e.g. edgeR quasi-likelihood) was run for a robustness cross-check, because the analysis is restricted to Python and no vetted Python-native equivalent is staged in this environment; this is a caveat on borderline calls, not a methodological requirement that was skipped by oversight.
acceptance_criteria: Three named contrasts are reported, each with the reference levels stated: (1) treatment drug vs vehicle within WT, (2) treatment drug vs vehicle within KO, (3) genotype:treatment interaction (difference of the drug effect between KO and WT)

Every gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, its standard error, shrunken log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj), computed with independent filtering within each contrast separately

MA plot and dispersion plot are produced for each of the two model fits (WT-reference and KO-reference)

State the method (PyDESeq2 version, design formula, explicit reference levels for genotype and treatment), the three named contrasts, the pre-filter and FDR thresholds (padj<0.05, BH, independent filtering), and the number of genes tested and DE per contrast, up front. Report shows QC and fit-diagnostic plots before any gene table

plan.title: Heart 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a balanced 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq experiment in heart tissue: genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), 4 replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, raw Salmon gene-level counts already summarized to gene symbols. The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype-by-treatment interaction question, so the core analysis fits a PyDESeq2 negative-binomial model with genotype, treatment, and their interaction, tests the interaction coefficient with a Wald test, and reports the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) alongside it, exactly as the interaction-design procedure prescribes. Because the user requires Python-only scripts, R-only tools (DESeq2 itself, ashr, edgeR) are replaced with PyDESeq2's native re-implementation: median-of-ratios normalization, Wald testing, Cook's-distance outlier flagging (relevant here since 4 replicates/cell is below the 7-replicate threshold where DESeq2/PyDESeq2 switches from flagging to replacing outliers), and apeglm-style native shrinkage. To get all three quantities (interaction, simple effect in WT, simple effect in KO) as single fitted coefficients — which is what PyDESeq2's shrinkage supports natively, avoiding a dependency on R's ashr for multi-coefficient contrasts — the model is fit twice with the genotype factor releveled (WT-reference and KO-reference), a standard way to extract each simple effect directly as a Wald coefficient. QC precedes the model (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to catch batch-like structure or outlier samples before trusting the fit; the metadata carries no batch variable, so no batch correction is planned. Enrichment runs per contrast (not pooled) on the full ranked gene list by the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome, the two curated pathway resources available for human in this environment, since the research question is about coordinated pathway-level divergence between genotypes as much as single-gene calls. No orthogonal DE method (edgeR/limma) is run, since Python has no directly equivalent vetted implementation staged in this environment and the user restricted execution to Python — this is stated as a caveat rather than worked around with an R call. No translational/safety/drug-repurposing steps are included because the research question and data context give no target, compound identity, PK/PD, or safety readouts to ground them.

Report the interaction-coefficient result as the formal statistical test of that difference, together with the caveat that power for this test is low at 4 replicates per cell. Present the per-contrast Hallmark and Reactome enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and compare which pathways are hit in the WT-simple-effect vs the KO-simple-effect vs the interaction contrast, again as a direct pathway-level read on genotype-dependent drug response. Close with a reproducibility record: package versions (pydeseq2, gseapy and their dependencies), any random seed used in the GSEA permutation test, and the gene-set collection versions/snapshot dates used. State plainly whether the data supports a genotype-dependent drug effect, a uniform drug effect regardless of genotype, or an inconclusive result, and say which of these is best supported and why, without overstating a result the interaction test's power cannot back up.
acceptance_criteria: Report states the design formula, both explicit reference levels, and all three contrast names with their meaning
Report shows QC and fit-diagnostic plots before any gene table
Report gives an explicit overlap/difference comparison between the WT-simple-effect and KO-simple-effect significant gene sets and between their enrichment hits
Report states the interaction-test result and its low-power caveat at n=4 per cell explicitly, and does not treat a non-significant interaction as proof of 'no genotype-dependent effect'
Report includes a reproducibility record (package versions, GSEA seed, gene-set collection versions/dates)
Report gives one direct, evidence-grounded answer to the research question with its confidence level and the reasons it is or is not fully conclusive
caveats: Do not present the interaction gene list or its enrichment as the primary evidence for genotype-dependent drug action if it is underpowered and near-empty — in that case the qualitative WT-vs-KO simple-effect comparison is the more informative evidence, and the report must say so.

grounding.reason: Interaction-design reporting rule (R-0092) requires the three results side by side with reference levels named; R-0041/R-0051/R-0086 set the reproducibility and method-reporting content of the final report.
